children: Nifty 50 began today’s session lower at 23,195 versus Wednesday’s close of 23,218. It recovered after opening and is now trading at 23,300, up about 0.3 per cent.

The advance/decline ratio of Nifty 50 now stands at 37/13, indicating a bullish inclination. HDFC Life (up 3.8 per cent) and Eternal (up 2.7 per cent) are the top gainers. Whereas ONGC (down 1.2 per cent) and HCL Technologies (down 1.1 per cent) are the top losers.

Among sectors, barring Nifty IT (down 0.5 per cent) all other indices are in the green, showing a broad-based buying. Nifty Midsmall Healthcare and Nifty Financial Service Ex-Bank, up 1.1 per cent each, are the top gainers.
While the above factors show positive indications, the chart of Nifty 50 and Nifty futures continue to exhibit weakness.
Nifty (Sep) futures began today’s session flat at 23,275 against yesterday’s close of 23,272. The contract rose after opening and is now trading at 23,350, up nearly 0.4 per cent.

The rise above 23,330, a minor resistance, is a bullish sign, at least for intraday. There is a chance for Nifty futures to see further rise, potentially to 23,500, a resistance. Subsequent barrier is at 23,600.
Instead, if the contract starts falling, it can drop to 23,250. A breach of this can intensify the sell-off, possibly leading to a swift decline to 23,200 and 23,100.
Nevertheless, as it stands, the bulls appears to have a slight edge over the bears.
Risk-averse traders can stay out. Traders with higher risk tolerance can buy Nifty (Sep) futures now at 23,350. Target and stop-loss can be 23,500 and 23,280 respectively.

title: Nifty Prediction Today – September 17, 2026: Nifty futures: Bulls might lift the contract intraday
